chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ayesha said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'The people of Bureyra stipulated the condition of her guardianship (walāʾ). So the Messenger of Allah said: 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates.'

key_terms.بَرِيرَة: Bureyra, a well-known freed slave woman in early Islamic history, Islamic history whose case clarified this legal ruling.
key_terms.وَلَاء: Guardianship or kinship by manumission; the right of the master to be considered a kin to the freed slave.

ai.seo_question: Who has the right of guardianship (walāʾ) over a freed slave in Islam?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal maxim that 'al-walāʾ liman aʿṭaq' (the right of manumission belongs to the one who frees), establishing that the patron's rights supersede any contractual stipulations made by the slave's original tribe. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is critical for determining inheritance and social obligations, as it prioritizes the act of emancipation over tribal lineage in the context of freed slaves. The narration highlights the Prophet's authority to override pre-Islamic customs, reinforcing the principle that manumission creates a new, binding legal kinship.
